newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel oil falls. Italian fuel demand stagnates.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel oil falls. Italian fuel demand stagnates.

text.p: European fuel oil markets were sickly on Wednesday as crude lost value and underlying demand was confirmed weak, traders said.
High sulphur fuel oil barges lost $1 to trade at $83 and $84 fob a tonne, with continuing poor bunker demand mostly to blame.
"I don't think crude has had much impact as fuel never rallied in the first place," said one trader. "It is more that there is clear oversupply on the prompt side because of the weak bunker demand."
Others said that Rotterdam's failure to take strength from Singapore confirmed that negative sentiment prevailed in Europe.
"If you look at prices in Singapore, which are solid, its really incredible what is happening here," said one trader. "Its not a good sign at all."
Crude's 35 cent fall on Wednesday after bearish U.S. stock data pressured one percent prices. Swaps lost $1 and physical prices were expected to follow.

Italian fuel consumption confirmed the poor demand that has driven cargo values sharply down this year. From Jan-Apr 1997 fuel consumption by the power generating sector fell 14 percent from last year at seven million tonnes, according to Italian Ministry of Industry figures provided by an industry source.

April consumption stood at 1.7 million tonnes, only one percent down on last year. One percent fuel accounted for 1.5 million tonnes, a 2.3 percent rise on April 1996, which was a month of historically low demand, the source said.

"It seems that the downward trend has eased," the source said. But he saw no improvement in the summer, with monthly fuel oil consumption at ENEL averaging just 1.7 million tonnes in the colder months.
